note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old female with several days of worsening, constant midline lower abdominal pain with associated light vaginal spotting and nausea; face-to-face abdominal/pelvic examination and repeat pregnancy test arranged.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Constant, severe lower midline abdominal pain below the umbilicus, present for a few days, worsening; pain rated approximately 8/10.
- Timeline:
  - Pain began a few days ago and has progressively worsened.
  - Last menstrual period approximately 2–3 weeks ago; patient states "my period stopped... last two weeks ago."
  - Light vaginal bleeding/spotting started after her last period and is ongoing (described as light pink).
  - Sexual intercourse occurred approximately 4 days ago.
  - Constipation for ~1 week last week; bowel function improved this week.
  - Pregnancy test performed about 1 month ago (result not documented); clinician advised repeat pregnancy test today.
  - Implanon implant inserted approximately 1 year ago.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Pain is constant and getting worse; no specific relieving factors mentioned.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Light vaginal bleeding/spotting (pink).
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - Recent constipation (resolved).
  - No fever or feeling feverish.
  - No vomiting, no fainting, no shoulder pain.
  - No dysuria, no urinary frequency/urgency reported.
  - Able to perform regular activities (work, cooking) though pain is very uncomfortable at times.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives (as mentioned):
  - No vomiting.
  - No fever or reported elevated temperature.
  - No shortness of breath.
  - No shoulder pain.
  - No urinary symptoms such as dysuria or haematuria reported.
  - No known weight loss reported.
  - No blood in stool reported.
  - No prior pregnancies.
  - No prior surgeries mentioned.

Past Medical History:
- Allergies:
  - Amoxicillin allergy (no reaction details provided).
- Medical conditions:
  - None otherwise reported.
- Surgical history:
  - No prior surgeries (patient reported none).
- Obstetric/Gynecologic:
  - No pregnancies to date.
  - Contraception: etonogestrel implant (Implanon) in place for ~1 year (dose/route/frequency not applicable / not documented).
- Current medications:
  - None documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: school teacher.
- Living situation: lives with husband and husband's family.
- Smoking/alcohol/substance use:
  - Smoking/drinking: patient answered "I don't know" when asked; status unclear.
  - Recreational drug use: patient denies.
- Travel:
  - Travel occurred about a year ago; no recent travel.
- No financial or lifestyle concerns documented.

Family History:
- No family history information provided in the consult.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Examination findings: no physical examination performed during the consult; face-to-face abdominal/pelvic examination proposed and patient consented.

Investigations:
- Pregnancy test:
  - Patient reports a pregnancy test approximately 1 month ago (result not documented).
  - Clinician requested a repeat pregnancy test today; advised urgent review if positive.
- No imaging or laboratory results documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal pain, midline, constant, worsening over days (approximately 8/10).
  - Assessment:
    - Acute lower abdominal pain of uncertain etiology; associated light vaginal spotting and nausea; recent intercourse and Implanon in situ. Specific diagnosis not established in this consult.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for formal abdominal and pelvic examination.
    - Patient advised to contact support line to book the face-to-face appointment.
    - Repeat pregnancy test today; if positive, patient to be seen immediately/urgently.
    - Advise earlier review/urgent care if symptoms markedly worsen, if unable to tolerate fluids, or if other red-flag symptoms develop.
- Issue 2: Light vaginal bleeding/spotting following recent period.
  - Assessment:
    - Spotting noted; etiology unclear (implant-related bleeding, gynecologic cause, pregnancy-related causes to be considered).
  - Plan:
    - Correlate with pelvic examination and pregnancy test result at face-to-face visit.
- Issue 3: Recent constipation (resolved).
  - Assessment:
    - Constipation lasted about one week last week and has since improved.
  - Plan:
    - No specific interventions documented; monitor bowel function.
- Issue 4: Allergy to amoxicillin.
  - Assessment:
    - Documented allergy; no reaction details recorded.
  - Plan:
    - Record allergy in medical record; avoid amoxicillin if prescribing antibiotics unless clarified.

- General plan items:
  - Patient to perform/obtain pregnancy test today and notify service.
  - Book and attend face-to-face clinic for abdominal and pelvic examination.
  - Seek earlier medical attention if condition deteriorates or if pregnancy test positive.
  - No medications or prescriptions were issued during this consult.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure) absent.
  - Results of prior pregnancy test (performed ~1 month ago) not documented.
  - No physical examination findings available.
  - No medication list or current prescriptions documented.
  - No details about the nature of amoxicillin allergy (type of reaction) recorded.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Travel history initially answered "Yes" then clarified as travel about a year ago; minor conflict noted.
  - Smoking/alcohol status unclear — patient responded "I don't know" when asked; status unknown.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Occasional audio difficulties and brief communication clarifications noted (patient initially stated she could not hear, and some responses required clarification). Overall intelligible; key clinical information was obtainable.
